transcript: There are only two people in this world that you need to make proud. Not your mom, not your dad, not your husband, not your wife, not even your kids. It's the eight-year-old version of you and the eighty-year-old version of you. If those two people are happy, then you did it right. Because the eight-year-old you, they didn't care about status. They didn't care about money or likes or titles. They cared about feeling safe, feeling alive, doing things that made their heart beat faster with joy. And the eighty-year-old you, they won't care about the mistakes you made. They won't care about the people who doubted you. They'll care about whether you lived bravely, whether you loved openly, whether you took the chances that scared you and said the things you always meant to say. Right now, you're caught somewhere in between. Caught in pressure, caught in expectation, caught in survival. But when you strip it all back, those two versions of you are still waiting. The child who dreamed and the elder who remembers live a life that makes both of them proud. Because in the end, they're the only ones who ever really mattered.
